title: The ready push makes the merge tree equal the head tree, so main's push run skips by the existing rule
why:
Source: the consultant's measured read at 12:15 CST Nov 14 (owner goal: CI speed, top priority), one tree pair re-read by the coordinator (coordinator 12:16, relayed; triage read none of it). Facts: REST read at 12:14: the last 8 main push `checks` runs each ran 30 of 33-35 jobs; the push skip fired 0 of 8. Cause as read: the merged tree never equals the green PR head tree (strict=false: the head is behind main at merge). The pair the coordinator read: #3402 head ef8582befd5f tree 2c29427dc8; merge 245e168db806 tree 28705afa96. Cost: a full run on main per merge (the run for 415e8b51b was still going at 31 min); its queued legs held the next ready mark (#3158 unmarked about 40 min). Proposal (the consultant's, no rule change): the ready-time records push becomes a merge of origin/main plus the records commit; if nothing merges during that PR's CI, the head tree equals the merge tree and main's push run skips by the existing rule (owner ruling push-skip-proven-tree, 12:18 CST Nov 13, item 729 a: skip the push re-run when the pushed tree equals the tree the PR tested). Risks the coordinator named in the lane's brief: a one-parent records commit after a record makes it stale (cost #3405 a fix check at 11:36), and overlap with #3396 (step records-page-before-ready, held on owner item 830). The standing grant lets the batch runner push a plain merge of main into a handed-in PR; each new head gets a fix verifier and a fresh review log. Related: owner item 830; steps records-page-before-ready, push-skip-proven-tree, tree-equal-skip-mutation-prs. Also asked: runner 11 reads the last 8 main push runs of home and degen the same way (they use the same push skip). Lane started 12:16 CST by the coordinator (session_013NEJKyzT11AdU32mgrLnAC) with a first deliverable before any build: design, the record-staleness answer, overlap with #3396, and whether an owner pick is needed; it stops there if one is. A guard-or-check change: if a verdict moves, round 3 applies. OWNER ITEM 840 12:20 CST Nov 14 (lane ready-push-merges-main via coordinator 12:18, relayed; triage read none of it): the lane built nothing and waits. Item 840 (pick-ready-push-merge-main) is on the page, linked to item 830. Making `merge <pr> --ready` push a merge of main widens what the merge tool does to a PR branch, and the records commit that `--ready` also pushes is a one-parent commit that makes the review record stale. Lane's code read: `draft_step` in merge/merge.py never pushes a merge today (`holds_base`, rule M3, lets a head lacking main's tip stand if the merge is clean); `live_review_state` ends its walk as stale at any one-parent commit, in either order; the lane-lint walk (about merge.py line 1861) already skips a page-only commit. One full checks run after the records step took 44 min (#3396's body, n=1). Options: a merge main at ready and the record skips page-only commits (widens; the lane recommends it; never starred), b merge main only and the record goes stale when the page changes, c leave it, d answer item 830 first (starred at the coordinator's recommendation, with b as its fallback). LABELS CORRECTED 12:23 CST Nov 14 (coordinator 12:18, from the lane, relayed): the lane labels option b too as going against the ruling and widening the merge tool (a pushed merge of main at ready is a new merge-tool write), and recommends c (leave it), the only option that widens nothing; it says a works if the owner puts CI speed above the ruling. The coordinator reads a as clearly widening what live_review_state accepts, and b and d as a change to one tool's own step that standing grant line 18 already allows by hand; it does not decide which reading holds. Triage applied the lane's count: item 840 (page version 2) marks a, b and d widens with the ruling line, stars none, and shows the coordinator's d and the lane's c in the context. ITEM 840 D REWORDED 12:24 CST Nov 14 (coordinator 12:19, relayed; its own reading from triage's wording of item 830, not from the item text or the code; the lane is asked to confirm from `draft_step` and `ready_page_state`): only 830 a (merge a ready green PR as is, refresh the page in a draft PR after) leaves `--ready` with no records commit. With 830 b or c the ready-time records push stays, a one-parent records commit follows a pushed merge of main, and the record goes stale as today: that is the option b fallback. Option d now says so (page version 3). DEGEN AND HOME READ 12:24 CST Nov 14 (runner 11 via coordinator 12:20; an Explore agent on Sonnet, REST job counts, trees by git against the merge commit's second parent; triage read none): DEGEN, last 8 main push `checks` runs: the push skip fired 2 of 8, on exactly the 2 merges whose merge tree equalled the PR head tree (#708 and #723; 5 jobs ok, 8 skipped); on the other 6 (17 ok, 2 skipped) the trees differed and it did not fire. all-jobs-passed and ci-done skip on all 8 (PR-only by design). HOME: no push-skip job in any of the 8 runs (7-8 jobs each, nothing skipped except ci-done once); all 8 merges had equal trees, so a skip could have applied to all 8. Unknown to runner 11: why home's ios job shows success with all steps skipped; what rule push-skip itself applies (its script lives in claude-settings, not read). So the cause the consultant read on claude-settings holds on degen: equal tree, the skip fires; moved main, it does not (2 of 8 against 0 of 8 here). LANE MEASURE 12:23 CST Nov 14 (the lane's read-only Sonnet agent via coordinator 12:21; neither the lane nor the coordinator re-read its rows; triage read none): of the last 15 merges to main (08:09 to 18:13 UTC today), 9 had one or more other merges to main between the ready run's start and the PR's own merge (13 other merges across the 9; #3404 had 2) and 6 had none. A merge of main at ready would leave head tree equal to merge tree for at most 6 of 15; the other 9 still mismatch. Ready-run length: median 39.4 min, range 29.7 to 79.0, n=15 (71.6 and 79.0 are #3279 and #3376). Unmeasured: the ready mark, pass or fail of each run, merges not among the 15. Unstudied additions by the lane: merging main right before the merge in the tool, or an owner pick on merge method (a squash gives no tree match either), would reach more than option a alone. CODE READ (the lane, merge/merge.py on main at 245e168; the coordinator did not re-read it): `draft_step` pushes one one-parent page commit (`commit_claim`, subject "Rebuild the records page", then `push_branch`) when `rebuild_records` changes the page; `ready_page_state` pushes nothing. Under 830 a, `--ready` pushes no page commit only if it stops rebuilding: a code change in `draft_step`, and the "stale page refused before any push" rule in the `--ready` docstring would go. Under 830 b it still pushes. Under 830 c it still pushes, and whether the PR run skips for a page-only commit is unknown (`page_only` serves the lane-lint walk; main's push skip judges tree equality, not commit shape). So option d's gain needs 830 a plus that code change. The coordinator leaves d unstarred and marked widens and does not claim d does not widen. All of this is in item 840 (page version 5).
